title: a no-substitution template literal is not a string literal, so it does not name a loader
notes: specification/comptime.mdx, 'Built-In Formats' (Locked): 'Non-code inputs MUST select their loader and mode with STANDARD import attributes', and docs/ASSET_LOADERS.md (Locked): 'Every non-code or foreign-source import uses standard import attributes. The required string-valued `type` selects its loader.' Standard import attributes are a closed shape, so the rules that keep them one shape belong to the language and not to a particular implementation's parser. `counter.json` really is staged and a JSON loader really is registered, so every one of these programs is refused for its attribute shape alone. The positive control is 23-asset-imports/a-json-import-selects-its-loader-with-an-import-attribute, which is the same file and the same loader with one well-formed `type` and must keep compiling and printing the file's own values. The near-miss the census missed and the Go port found: a no-substitution template literal has the same TEXT as the string literal beside it, and a predicate spelled `isStringLiteralLike` matches it while `isStringLiteral` does not. Accepting it puts a template into loader selection and into the asset identity key, which is the same admission hole as the computed identifier reached through a different predicate — so it is pinned as its own case rather than folded into 23-asset-imports/a-computed-import-attribute-value-is-rejected. Same two-code cascade, same reason.
